en.short_description: Turn-by-turn routes, nearby hazard alerts, and public safety radio links.
en.description:
iMaps is a dark-themed navigation app. It combines worldwide turn-by-turn driving routes with one-tap incident reporting on your map, a live feed of official hazard alerts within two miles of you, and links to public safety and air traffic radio where available — in one app, in fifteen languages.

—— Navigation ——

Worldwide driving routes and step-by-step guidance, powered by OSRM (Open Source Routing Machine). Enter a destination and follow a clear, high-contrast route built for night driving. Turn instructions are shown in your language.

—— Incident reports ——

Mark what you see — accidents, police, road hazards, heavy traffic — on your map in one tap, with five seconds to undo. Reports lose severity automatically over time, so a stale report quietly fades instead of misleading you. Reports are kept on your device; sharing reports with other drivers is not available yet, and the app says so.

—— A two-mile alert radius ——

iMaps aggregates four public data sources and shows only what is genuinely near you:

• USGS — local earthquakes, magnitude 1.0 and above, past 24 hours
• NOAA / National Weather Service — active severe weather alerts
• GDACS — global disaster alerts for cyclones, floods, wildfires and volcanoes
• Open311 — municipal reports such as potholes and signal outages, in supported cities

—— Public safety radio ——

Find the public-safety scanner streams that OpenMHz and Radio Browser list near you, and air traffic control feeds from LiveATC, and open them in your browser or audio app, with a link to your local NOAA Weather Radio information. Coverage depends on what those services list for your area; where they list nothing, the app says so.

—— Fifteen languages ——

Available in English, Spanish, Mandarin, Hindi, French, Arabic, German, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean, Italian, Russian, Turkish, Indonesian and Swahili. Turn-by-turn directions, the tab bar and the core map and alert screens are translated; some screens and labels are still in English.

—— Companion browser extension ——

An optional Chrome, Edge and Firefox extension mirrors live events and radio streams in your browser.

—— About your location ——

iMaps needs your location to route you and to decide which alerts are within two miles. It uses your location only while the app is open. Your position is used to query public feeds and is not sold. The app shows ads through Google AdMob. Full detail is in the privacy policy linked from this listing.

Drive attentively. Please do not interact with the app while your vehicle is moving.

en.release_notes:
First public release of iMaps.

• Worldwide turn-by-turn driving routes powered by OSRM, with instructions in your language
• One-tap incident reporting on your map with automatic severity decay
• Two-mile live alert radius from USGS, NOAA/NWS, GDACS and Open311
• Links to public safety and air traffic radio from OpenMHz, Radio Browser and LiveATC, where available
• Fifteen languages
• Companion browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox

Feedback is welcome at contact@americangroup.ai.

review_information.notes:
2. DEVICES AND OS VERSIONS TESTED
Automated tests run on every build: iPhone 17 Pro Max and iPad Pro 13-inch simulators on iOS 26, and a Pixel Android emulator on API 34.
Each release is also installed and launched on those targets, so a
build that cannot start never ships.

3. WHAT THIS APP DOES, AND FOR WHOM
iMaps is a dark-themed navigation app. It combines worldwide turn-by-turn driving routes with one-tap incident reporting on your map, a live feed of official hazard alerts within two miles of you, and links to public safety and air traffic radio where available — in one app, in fifteen languages.

Incident reports are stored on the device only; this build has no shared community backend, and the Alerts feed, report sheet and Settings say so.

Intended audience:
Traffic, alerts & live radio

4. SETTING UP AND REACHING THE MAIN FEATURES
On first launch the app shows a three-page introduction and asks for location while in use; after that it opens on the guest home screen (map). No account is needed; every feature works without signing in. Sign-in is optional and is reached from the profile header at the top of the You tab (bottom bar, right-most). The demo account below can be used there.

5. EXTERNAL SERVICES USED
- Supabase — optional account sign-in
- Google AdMob — advertising
- Google Sign-In — authentication
- Sign in with Apple — authentication
- device location services (on-device, while in use)
- Public data APIs over HTTPS: OSRM (routing), Nominatim (search), CARTO / OpenStreetMap (map tiles), USGS, NOAA/NWS, GDACS, Open311, OpenStreetMap Overpass, Open-Meteo, OpenMHz, Radio Browser, LiveATC
- Radio streams open in the browser or the device's audio app; the app has no built-in audio player

6. REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
The app ships 15 languages (Arabic, Chinese (Simplified), English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, id, sw, tr). Features are identical in every region.

7. REGULATED INDUSTRY OR THIRD-PARTY MATERIAL

The app is not in a regulated industry. Map data is © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) and basemap tiles are © CARTO; both are credited on every map. Alert content comes from the public feeds listed in section 5 and is attributed to its source. All other content, artwork and copy are the developer's own.


ACCOUNT DELETION
When signed in, account deletion is on the You tab ('Delete account', the last row), and on the support site.
